name: Akira Mori
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1999-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Akira Mori is the chairman and owner of real estate developer Mori Trust.
Mori Trust owns more than 100 properties in Tokyo and across Japan, including office buildings and hotels.
His daughter, Miwako Date, is president and CEO of Mori Trust. She plans to invest nearly $8 billion in new projects, with about 20% going overseas.
In 2023, Mori Trust opened two new hotels in Japan, one in Tokyo and another in the ancient capital of Nara.
In 2025, it acquired partial ownership of a large mixed-use building that includes office, hotel and retail spaces in Manhattan.
forbes_facts: In 2023, the firm bought close to a 50% stake in a 45-story New York office tower on Park Avenue, costing $700 million.

name: Ji Qi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2021)
forbes_bio: Ji Qi is the founder and executive chairman of H World Group, one of China's biggest multi-brand hotel groups.
H World Group operates over 13,000 hotels globally under a variety of brands, such as Hi Inn and eponymous Ji Hotel, with a focus on the budget and midscale segments.
Once known as China Lodging Group and Huazhu Group, the company trades on both the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and Nasdaq.
Ji also cofounded Trip.com, one of China's largest travel booking site.

name: Sam Altman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); SEC insider holdings (2024); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Sam Altman is the CEO of OpenAI and a prolific venture investor.
In 2005, he dropped out of Stanford to found social mapping company Loopt, which sold in 2012 for $43 million; he used proceeds to seed his own venture fund.
Around that time, Altman became a partner at startup accelerator Y Combinator, then served as YC's president from 2014 to 2019.
That year, Altman left YC to become CEO of OpenAI, now worth some $500 billion, although he was briefly fired and rehired in 2023.
He has no equity in OpenAI, and instead owes his wealth to his investments, including stakes in Stripe, Reddit and nuclear fusion firm Helion.

name: Ye Qiongjiu

forbes_bio: Ye Qiongjiu is deputy general manager of Hithink RoyalFlush Information Network, an online financial information services business.
Ye cofounded the predecessor business of Hithink with its chairman and fellow billionaire Yi Zheng.
Hithink founded Hithinkin Hangzhou in 1994 with 100,000 yuan, currently worth $14,000; it went public in 2009.

name: J. Frank Harrison III
forbes_bio: J. Frank Harrison, III is the long-time chairman and CEO of Coca-Cola Consolidated, the largest independent Coca-Cola bottler in the U.S.
He owns 15% of the publicly traded company, which his great-grandfather J.B. Harrison founded in 1902, but has majority voting control.
He succeeded his father J. Frank Harrison, Jr. (d. 2002) as CEO in 1994 and chairman in 1996.
A graduate of the University of North Carolina and Duke MBA, he joined the Charlotte-based company in 1977 and got his start running routes and operating bottling lines.
A devout Christian, he cofounded a missionary organization called Open Eyes with his son James Harrison IV, who died while doing relief work in Kenya in 2010.

name: Sharron Hunt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Sharron Hunt owns the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs with her three siblings. Her brother Clark is chairman and CEO.
Their father Lamar Hunt (d. 2006) founded the team and passed control to his kids in 2005. Lamar is credited with naming the Super Bowl.
Forbes estimates the Chiefs are now worth more than $4.7 billion (net of debt). Each Hunt Sibling owns an estimated 25% stake.
The Hunt siblings also own MLS team FC Dallas and a minority stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls. Clark is chairman and CEO of the family's soccer club, while brother Dan is president.
Lamar was one of 11 heirs of oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt (d. 1974) who appeared on the first ever Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans in 1982.
